finding: The fourth no-rows cause dropped its empty-stored-hash exemption this revision, justified by: "The comparison is plain inequality with no exemption for an empty stored hash: the only rounds carrying one predate the corpus feature, and their rows carry no role, so they end every streak by the rule above regardless." Both halves of that premise are false against the tree. `engine.ComputeRolesHash` returns `("", err)` when a role file exists but cannot be read (internal/engine/rolehash.go:59-62), and both audit callers discard the error — `rolesHash, _ := engine.ComputeRolesHash(...)` at internal/cli/audit_record.go:106 (record) and :187 (status). A round recorded while one `.tp/auditors/*.json` is unreadable therefore stores `roles_hash: ""` while postdating the corpus feature and carrying fully role-attributed rows. The consequence for §6 test 11 is concrete: its second half ("a round carrying an empty stored hash beside rounds carrying a non-empty one also ends the streak") is only discriminating over a fixture whose empty-hash round holds role-bearing PASS rows, which is exactly the state §2.1 declares impossible. A tester who follows §2.1's premise builds a roleless empty-hash round, whose streak already ends by §2.2's rule, and the assertion then passes identically against an implementation that kept the exemption — the same non-discriminating shape as the round-7 finding this revision was fixing, in mirror image.

finding: §2.1 pins the `status` predicate byte-for-byte and the `role` predicate as "whitespace-trimmed", but leaves "non-blank line" undefined: "a round contributes no rows when ... any **non-blank** line in it fails to unmarshal into a JSON map" plus "Blank lines are skipped before parsing". Two readings are available — `line == ""` and `strings.TrimSpace(line) == ""` — and they diverge on a CRLF-terminated results file: splitting on "\n" leaves a bare "\r" for each blank line, which the raw reading treats as a non-blank line that fails to unmarshal, so the round contributes no rows. The record path (countAuditFindings) trims before the blank test and therefore accepts such a file, which breaks §2.1's own stated guarantee that "Matching the record path is what keeps the two from disagreeing about a file tp itself accepted": on a CRLF-authored results file the streaks would be permanently 0/`null` and `divergence` could never fire, with no observable cause but the advisory.

finding: §2.1 requires one advisory "naming which of the four causes applies", but the four no-rows causes are not mutually exclusive and no precedence is stated. After a corpus edit between rounds every earlier round carries a differing stored `roles_hash`; if such a round also has a deleted file, an empty `file` entry, or an unparseable line, two causes apply to the same round and the spec does not say which of the two table wordings is emitted. Test 9 exercises one cause per fixture and cannot pin the choice.

finding: §2.1's fourth cause justifies plain inequality on `roles_hash` with "the only rounds carrying one [an empty stored hash] predate the corpus feature, and their rows carry no role, so they end every streak by the rule above regardless". That invariant does not hold today: a phase with no user role files hashes to the sentinel "builtin" (not ""), while both record paths swallow the error return — `rolesHash, _ := engine.ComputeRolesHash(...)` — so a round recorded while any `.tp/auditors/*.json` is listed but unreadable is stored with an empty hash and rows that do carry roles. Such a round then reads as "recorded under a different auditor corpus" although the corpus never moved, terminating the walk and emitting a misleading advisory (the direction is conservative, so no signal is invented, but the stated reason for accepting the rule is wrong and an implementer may take it as licence to shortcut the empty case).

finding: The `open` field of a `role_streaks` entry is defended nowhere as a magnitude. §2.2 line 67 argues the reverse direction only (that `consecutive_clean` earns its place beside `open`), and concedes that `open == 0` and `consecutive_clean >= 1` are the same condition — so `open`'s boolean content is already carried by the sibling field. Its numeric content is a per-role non-PASS tally of the latest round, which on `--record` is a tally of the very file the driver just handed tp in this invocation, and which on `--status` is re-derivable from `divergence`'s counted fields for the state that matters. §2.4 line 119 then argues at length that no reader should have to join arrays and difference counts — yet `open` is precisely the raw material for that discouraged derivation.
